articles.detail: 5 cycles, 5 completed; 11/12/13/14/13 stories selected against targets of 11/12/13/15/15, 56 published (11/10/12/10/13), of which 50 carry today's date and 6 from the 05:00 and 10:00 cycles carry 2026-10-07; 0 quarantined

experiment: Skipped. No experiment is active, and the pause gate (`noNewExperimentsUntil` 2026-11-05, set today while the cycle runner is restructured) bars a new one; nothing was evaluated or changed.
weakestArea: US datelines are 28% against 25%, the fifth-cycle cause being supply: at 22:00 all three tech picks were US because the feed held no non-US tech story, and a fourth US pick was taken to keep economy above its floor. Latin America is 4% against 5% (São Paulo and Medellín counted; the Culiacán story may not have been, which would make it 6%), still with no Latin American outlet in any feed. Multi-source recovered to 32% from 27%, but the 18:00 and 22:00 cycles again missed both multi-source floors (politics 0 of 2 twice, economy 0 and 1).
watching: Iran: the Pentagon is drafting strike options before the US midterms while Hormuz traffic is at a two-month low and a tanker was hit by projectiles north of Qatar.
Saudi Arabia: oil surged after Houthi strikes on Riyadh, and a coalition strike in Sanaa killed a schoolgirl.
Ukraine: strikes killed at least 38 and hit a Yandex data centre, and a guided bomb hit a Kramatorsk bus stop with tolls of 12 and 33 in different sources.
Israel shut Britain's East Jerusalem consulate and expelled 20 diplomats.
India: the Reserve Bank's repo rise, the tax council scrapping an arrest power and the Starlink clearance made three picks in one cycle.
Brazil: Bolsonaro's pension pledge follows Sunday's first-round vote; the B3 market comment was rejected for asserting a cause.
Russia: the plague-lab follow-up was removed as a fuzzy duplicate of the 10-07 Trump-Putin story, so the unanswered question has not run.
Broadcom's 7.2% move went unexplained by the feed in all five cycles.
coverageGaps: At 22:00, 14 of 26 RSS feeds and Hacker News timed out (404 Media, SciDev.Net, Carbon Brief, Rest of World, The Diplomat, Dialogue Earth, Global Voices among them), leaving 35 RSS stories and no HN, in the first cycle after the one-retry change landed.
Science was 0 against 2 at 05:00 and 1 against 2 at 18:00; the 05:00 feed held two dataset descriptors and a paper whose text was a conflict-of-interest statement.
Tech had nothing usable from Ars Technica, The Register, The Decoder or Hacker News at 05:00 and 10:00, and no non-US tech story at 22:00.
Economy fell to 2 against 3 after dedup at 18:00, the second day running a late cycle ended there.

The 18:00 selection of 14 reached the writer as 10: three picks were dropped as sourceless after the page fetch (one still thin, two whose fetched text was about something else) and one as a duplicate.
Thin picks were recovered for 4 of 9 sources across the first four cycles, and for 0 of 1 at 10:00.
Bloomberg page fetches failed again (source-angles, 05:00 and 14:00), and the selector is skipping Bloomberg items because of it.
Oceania had no dateline and no candidate in any cycle; no Latin American outlet appeared in the feed.
Dawn supplied six articles, two of them on Pakistani wheat policy.
Freshness was measured on 1 of 50 articles, so the 0-day median is not a reading of the day.
context: All five cycles completed in an average of 869s (selector 197s, writer 248s, editor 85s). State-or-advocacy-only stories fell from five to one (Dodik's party in Bosnia) and nothing was quarantined. For the operator: check whether the 22:00 feed timeouts were one network event or a side effect of the RSS retry change committed at 20:33, since a repeat would cut science and tech supply; the MercoPress addition to CURATED_SOURCES remains the first experiment to run once the gate lifts on 2026-11-05, after its Event Registry URI is verified. Odds rows were offered in four cycles (9 rows).
